h2: NDT training near Honolulu: the shipyard apprenticeship, mainland college programmes and online study compared
html:
NDT training near Honolulu: the shipyard apprenticeship, mainland college programmes and online study compared

From Oahu, a search for "NDT training near me" has an unusual answer: the one structured local route into NDT is a shipyard apprenticeship, and every full college programme we found is across the Pacific. The list above names the main local players; this section goes further into how each route works in practice, what it costs you in time away from the islands, and which one suits which candidate.

Who offers NDT training for Honolulu candidates?

  • Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard and IMF apprentice programme. The shipyard's apprenticeship page lists Non-Destructive Tester (NDT) as a Quality Assurance trade. The programme takes four years and requires at least 7,200 hours across on-the-job training, trade theory and academic study, and it is full-time federal employment from the start. Apprentices attend academic courses at Pearl Harbor one week a month during the programme's opening two years, and graduates receive a tuition-free Applied Trades degree from Honolulu Community College. Openings depend on the shipyard's needs and are posted on USAJOBS.
  • Clover Park Technical College, Lakewood, Washington. A degree in nondestructive testing of about eight quarters, plus single-method certificates in eddy current, MT and PT, radiography and ultrasonics. For an islander this is the most complete college option we verified, though it means moving to the mainland for the length of the course.
  • Linn-Benton Community College, Albany, Oregon. A two-year AAS in Nondestructive Testing and Evaluation with hands-on phased array, radiography, penetrant, magnetic particle and visual work.
  • Southern California. The American Aerospace Technical Academy in Los Angeles runs a ten-week, 400-hour programme across PT, MT, UT, RT and VT with introductions to phased array and digital radiography. It is the shortest full-time option we found, and still more than two months away from home.
  • Island employers. Inspection firms serving the harbours, Kalaeloa and Barbers Point industry and construction train some staff in-house under their own written practices.

Which route fits a Honolulu candidate?

SituationRoute that fitsWhat it asks of you
Young candidate wanting a long shipyard careerThe shipyard apprenticeshipFour years, a federal hiring process and the shipyard's own qualification rules
Newcomer free to leave Oahu for a whileA mainland college degree or certificateMonths or quarters off-island, then a job search back home
Technician already employed in HawaiiSelf-paced theory and a practical at your employerSupervised experience hours logged at work
Hawaii employer qualifying a crewTraining brought to your site against your written practiceA Level III to prepare, administer and grade the exams

Questions to ask any provider when you train from Hawaii

  • Hours. Does the record give classroom hours per method and level that meet SNT-TC-1A's recommendation? The hours planner shows the targets.
  • The practical. If the course is on the mainland, where will you do the hands-on work, and on what specimens?
  • Certification. Your employer certifies you under its written practice; shipyard qualification follows the Navy's own rules, so moving later to commercial work means certifying again with the new employer.
  • Acceptance. Will the island employer you want accept the training record, or train you its own way?
  • Support across time zones. When can you actually reach the Level III with a question?

Where Atlantis fits for Honolulu candidates and employers

The Atlantis route removes the flight. Theory is studied on the Atlantis portal from the day you enrol, at your own pace, with written questions answered by an ASNT NDT Level III. The Practical NDT simulator runs in a browser for set-up and scanning practice, and the hands-on practical and practical exam take place at your employer's facility on Oahu, on its equipment, under a written practice built on SNT-TC-1A; the employer certifies. For harbour, tank and structural work, ultrasonic testing training, magnetic particle testing training and visual testing training are the usual set; newcomers start at NDT Level 1 training.

Island companies can have training delivered on-site for a whole crew, with exams under their written practice, through SNT-TC-1A training programme set-up. Related pages: NDT training across Hawaii, Los Angeles and Seattle.
